content.title: About
content.content: Cherries are the edible fruits of the sweet cherry tree (Prunus cerasus), native to temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere. Raw cherries are bright red, have a tart‑sweet flavor and a juicy texture. They are eaten fresh, used in cooking, baking, desserts, and for making juices and preserves.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cherries belong to the Rosaceae family and are closely related to plums, apricots, and almonds.
There are over 400 cherry varieties, differing in taste, color, and harvest time.
Raw cherries are rich in antioxidants, especially anthocyanins, which give them their vivid red hue.
Cherry juice has been traditionally used in folk medicine to improve circulation.
Cherries were among the first fruits cultivated by the ancient Romans.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Cherries provide a substantial amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Anthocyanins and polyphenols in cherries help combat free radicals and may reduce the risk of chronic diseases.

items.title: Heart‑healthy
items.content: Potassium and fiber in cherries contribute to normal blood pressure and improve lipid profiles.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Fiber promotes intestinal motility and helps maintain regular bowel movements.

items.title: Contains melatonin
items.content: Cherries naturally contain melatonin, a hormone that regulates sleep, which may support better rest.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cherries, manifesting as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Raw cherries contain natural sugars, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidic nature of cherries can irritate the stomach lining in those with heightened sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw cherries can be enjoyed as a snack, added to oatmeal, yogurt, salads, baked goods, or used to make sauces and compotes. If desired, pits can be removed with specialized tools.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cherries in the refrigerator in an airtight container, where they stay fresh for 7‑10 days. For longer storage, freeze the berries in a single layer on a tray, then transfer to a freezer bag.

pasta-whole-grain-with-cream-sauce-ready.title: Whole Grain Pasta with Cream Sauce, Ready‑to‑Heat

content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain pasta with cream sauce is a ready‑to‑heat meal that combines whole‑grain noodles with a rich, dairy‑based cream sauce. The product is designed for quick preparation: simply heat in the microwave or on the stovetop and enjoy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain pasta retains the bran and germ, providing more fiber and micronutrients than refined pasta.
The cream sauce is typically made from milk, cream, and a modest amount of cheese for a smooth texture.
Convenient packaging allows a fast meal without sacrificing flavor or nutritional value.
Whole grain pasta has a lower glycemic index compared with traditional white pasta.
Packaging is usually microwave‑safe, eliminating the need to transfer the food to another container.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Whole grain pasta supplies both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion and stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Complex carbohydrates provide sustained energy, making the meal suitable for active days.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Whole grains are a good source of B1, B3, and B6 vitamins, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D from the sauce
items.content: The cream sauce adds calcium and, when fortified, vitamin D, contributing to bone health.

items.title: Low in trans fats
items.content: When produced correctly, the sauce contains no trans fats, making the product more heart‑friendly.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The cream sauce contains dairy; individuals with lactose intolerance should choose lactose‑free alternatives.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Ready‑to‑heat meals can be calorie‑dense due to cream and cheese; portion control is advisable for weight management.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: The sauce often includes salt; people monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Wheat allergy / gluten
items.content: The pasta is wheat‑based and may trigger reactions in those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the package in the microwave (typically 2–3 minutes) or on the stovetop, stir, let stand for a minute, and serve. Enhance the dish with fresh herbs, grated Parmesan, or steamed vegetables for added flavor and nutrition.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened package in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, keep the remaining product refrigerated and consume within 2–3 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Whiskey and water is a classic cocktail in which pure whiskey is diluted with clean drinking water. This method of serving allows the aromatic notes of the spirit to unfold, softens the strength, and highlights the flavor nuances characteristic of the specific whiskey variety.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The tradition of adding water to whiskey dates back to 18th‑century Scotland, when water was used to reduce the “burn” of strong spirits.
The optimal water‑to‑whiskey ratio is usually 1:1‑2, but varies according to personal taste and the type of whiskey.
Water is often served at room temperature to avoid “condensing” aromatic compounds.
Many experts recommend mineral or filtered water to avoid altering the drink’s flavor with impurities.
Whiskey and water is typically served in small tumblers or glasses that allow observation of the drink’s color change.

items.title: Reduced stomach irritation
items.content: Diluting whiskey with water lowers the alcohol concentration, which can lessen the irritating effect on the stomach lining.

items.title: Enhanced aroma perception
items.content: Water releases hidden aromatic compounds, allowing a more complete appreciation of the spirit’s complex bouquet.

items.title: Better control of alcohol intake
items.content: Dilution lets you sip more slowly and enjoy the flavor longer, supporting moderate consumption.

items.title: Alcohol intoxication
items.content: Even when diluted, whiskey remains an alcoholic beverage; excessive consumption carries the same risks as drinking straight whiskey.

items.title: Interaction with medications
items.content: Alcohol can amplify the effects of certain drugs; limit or avoid consumption when taking medication.

items.title: Water quality
items.content: Using water high in chlorine or heavy metals can degrade taste and potentially harm health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour 30‑50 ml of whiskey into a glass, add an equal or double amount of water to taste, and stir gently. Sip in small mouthfuls, allowing the drink to rest for a few minutes so the aroma fully develops.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the whiskey bottle in a cool, dark place away from direct sunlight and temperature fluctuations. The water for dilution should be fresh, preferably filtered, and kept in a sealed container.

content.title: About
content.content: Plain yogurt made from low‑fat milk contains minimal fat (typically 0.1‑0.5%). It has a mild, creamy flavor, smooth texture, and provides a good source of protein, calcium, and probiotic cultures.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Low‑fat yogurt retains most nutrients of whole milk while drastically reducing fat content.
Probiotics in yogurt support gut health and may boost immunity.
In many countries plain yogurt is used as a base for sauces, marinades, and desserts.
Compared with regular yogurt, the low‑fat version cools faster and feels lighter on the palate.
Low‑fat yogurt is often recommended in weight‑loss diets.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: A 200 ml serving provides about 10 g of high‑quality protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Yogurt supplies over 15 % of the daily calcium requirement, essential for bones and teeth.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: The reduced fat content makes it suitable for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Probiotic cultures
items.content: Live Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium strains help maintain a balanced gut microbiome.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience discomfort, although probiotics can mitigate symptoms.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein or whey requires complete avoidance of yogurt.

items.title: Added sugar in some brands
items.content: Even “plain” yogurts may contain added sugars; check the label if you monitor sugar intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy yogurt as a snack, blend into smoothies, use as a base for dressings, sauces, desserts, or substitute for sour cream in recipes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep yogurt refrigerated at 1‑4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5‑7 days and do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
